Reuters Does A Great Story On The Berlin Hemp Parade:
50,000 Call For Legalization.

Of course, the fact that it moved on the Reuters wire does not mean that any DEAland papers are likely to carry it. However, the fact that Reuters Television reported on the parade means that it must have had some coverage in Europe.

The Germans are still very sensitive to DEAland pressure, but there is an incremental weakening in their marijuana laws.)

August 31, 1999
From Reuters

THOUSANDS OF GERMANS CALL FOR LEGALISATION OF CANNABIS

BERLIN, Aug 28 (Reuters) - More than 50,000 people took part in Berlin's third annual ``Hemp Parade'' on Saturday, taking to the streets of the German capital to call for the legalisation of cannabis.

Carrying posters urging politicians to legalise the drug, the demonstrators called for a relaxation of laws on its possession.

"The German law is stupid in many points and we are demanding complete legalisation...for medical and recreational uses,'' said Martin Muencheberg, a press spokesman for the parade's organisers

``Even in the world's oldest medicine book there is a report of (its) medicinal uses,'' he told Reuters Television. "And throughout history, studies prove that THC, the active agent in cannabis, has many therapeutic and pain-relieving qualities.''

The participants, who came from all age groups, were demonstrating against what they called "state repression.''

(Marijuananews note: This is a subject on which the German people can speak with some experience.)

Cannabis is still regarded as an illegal drug in Germany although posession of small amounts is no longer considered a crime.

(Marijuananews note: Personal possession was decriminalized at the federal level, but the different German states have different limits, more in the Northwest, a few grams in Bavaria. The Germans have also adopted Dutch indoor growing techniques and – ironically -- it may be safer to run a large grow in Germany than in Holland. The Germans place more restrictions on their police than do the Dutch.)

Thirty floats paraded from Berlin's central Alexanderplatz square to the historic Brandenburg Gate

The hemp plant can also be used for such diverse articles as ropes, textiles, beer and cosmetics.
